questions.text:
f(x) = 4x³ – 3x² + 5x + 2.

Use calculus to find the gradient of f(x) at x = 2.

f'(x) = 6 – 4x + 12x².

The graph of f(x) passes through the point (1, 9).

Find f(x).

The equation of a curve is y = 2x³ – 9x² – 24x + 5.

Find the x-coordinate of the local minimum.
questions.markingGuide: dy/dx = 6x² – 18x – 24 = 6(x² – 3x – 4) = 6(x – 4)(x + 1). Set dy/dx = 0: x = 4 or x = –1. d²y/dx² = 12x – 18. At x = 4: 12(4) – 18 = 30 > 0, so x = 4 is a local minimum. (At x = –1: 12(–1) – 18 = –30 < 0, so x = –1 is a local maximum.) Merit = correct identification with justification.

questions.text: Explain how you know x = 4 is a minimum.
questions.markingGuide: d²y/dx² = 12x – 18. At x=4: 30 > 0 (minimum). At x=–1: –30 < 0 (maximum). Excellence = correct identification and justification.

questions.text:
A manufacturer wants to design a cylindrical tin (with lid) that holds 500 mL and minimises the surface area.

Calculate the optimal dimensions.

Volume: V = πr²h. Surface area: SA = 2πr² + 2πrh.

The graph of y = g(x) is a downward-opening parabola with vertex at (3, 5) and x-intercepts at (1, 0) and (5, 0).

Sketch the graph of y = g'(x).
questions.expectedAnswer: A straight line sloping downward, crossing x-axis at x = 3.
questions.markingGuide: g(x) is a downward parabola so g'(x) is a negatively-sloped line. g'(x) = 0 at x = 3 (vertex). g'(x) > 0 for x < 3, g'(x) < 0 for x > 3. Achieved = correct shape or intercept. Merit = both correct.

questions.text: Find the equation of the tangent to g(x) = 4 – 6x + 3x³ at the point (–1, 7).

A virus spreads through a community. The number of infected people is modelled by:

N(t) = t³ – 54t² + 720t + 5000

where N is the number infected and t is days after the outbreak.

Find the rate at which infection is changing on day 10.
questions.markingGuide: N'(t) = 3t² – 108t + 720. N'(10) = 300 – 1080 + 720 = –60. Decreasing at 60 people per day.

questions.text:
Use calculus to determine the difference in infected population from the start of the outbreak to when the epidemic begins to grow again.

N(t) = t³ – 60t² + 768t + 20000.
questions.expectedAnswer: 4096 fewer people (N(0) = 20000, N(32) = 15904, so population drops by 4096 before growing again)

questions.text:
A trapezium is drawn within the parabola y = 8x – x² and the x-axis. The parallel sides are at x = a and x = 2a, where 0 ≤ a ≤ 4.

Use calculus to find the maximum area of the trapezium.
questions.markingGuide: Heights at x = a and x = 2a: y₁ = 8a – a², y₂ = 16a – 4a². Width of trapezium = 2a – a = a. Area A = ½(y₁ + y₂) × a = ½(24a – 5a²) × a = 12a² – (5/2)a³. A'(a) = 24a – (15/2)a² = a(24 – 15a/2) = 0. Reject a = 0. Then 24 = 15a/2, so a = 48/15 = 16/5 = 3.2 (within 0 ≤ a ≤ 4). A(3.2) = 12(10.24) – 2.5(32.768) = 122.88 – 81.92 = 40.96. Check A''(a) = 24 – 15a; at a = 3.2, A'' = 24 – 48 = –24 < 0, confirming a maximum. Maximum area ≈ 40.96. Excellence = correct maximum with calculus working and verification.

questions.text:
h(x) = 0.5x² – 4x + 3.

Find the coordinate where the gradient of h(x) equals 5.

A cyclist starts from rest at an intersection. She accelerates at a constant rate of 1.2 m/s² until she reaches her top speed of 12 m/s.

Find the distance the cyclist has travelled when she reaches her top speed.

A gradient function f'(x) = x + 3 is shown on a graph (a straight line through (–3, 0) with gradient 1).

(i) Find f(x) which passes through (3, 0).
(ii) Describe key features of f(x).
questions.expectedAnswer: f(x) = 0.5x² + 3x – 13.5. Roots at x = –9 and x = 3, minimum at (–3, –18).

questions.text:
Two positive numbers x and y satisfy y = k – x, where k is a positive constant.

W = x² + 5y². Use calculus to find the minimum value of W in terms of k.
